description.narrative: Livability and climate resilience in selected cities in priority industrial corridors enhanced.

600 ha. of flood-prone areas covered by new drainage systems adapted to climate change and flood risk reduced in one city (Thoothukudi) (2021 baseline: 0) Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Collection and treatment of sewage in project coverage areas of one city (Coimbatore) increased to 100% of households (2021 baseline: sewage collected from 0% of households in coverage areas) Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Frequency and duration of water supply improved to 24 hours/day for 100% of households in coverage areas in one city (Madurai) (2021 baseline: water provided on average 1-2 hours/day, once in 1-2 days, 94% piped water coverage) Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:
Nonrevenue water in coverage areas in one city (Madurai) reduced to 20% (2021 baseline: 30%) Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Climate resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in two cities (Coimbatore and Thoothukudi). Indicator: 14 sewage pump and lift stations with combined capacity of 348 kW added in Coimbatore (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 3.1.3; OP 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Works are in progress in 17 sewage pump and lift stations Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in two cities (Coimbatore and Thoothukudi). Indicator: 36 km of new tertiary stormwater drains constructed with GESI-responsivee climate-resilient designs in Thoothukudi (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 2.5.2; OP 3.2.1; OP 4.3.1) Progress/Status: Works Completed.​
36.36 km of storm water drain has been constructed. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in two cities (Coimbatore and Thoothukudi). Indicator: 529 km of new sewage collection pipelines commissioned and connected to 67,545 households in Coimbatore, including 100% of the poord households in the coverage area (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 2.1.4; OP 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Works are in progress. 239.80 km of sewer lines has been laid and 15429 HSCs have been provided. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in two cities (Coimbatore and Thoothukudi). Indicator: Two all-female SHGsf trained (one each in Madurai and Coimbatore) and 80% of trained members reported improved knowledge on benefits of household connection to sewage collection system, sanitation, health and hygiene, water conservation and in areas of leadershipg (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.1) Progress/Status: Will be complied. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in two cities (Coimbatore and Thoothukudi). Indicator: Two new STPs with total capacity of 34.92 MLD added in Coimbatore (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 3.3.1, OP 3.3.2, OP 4.1.2) Progress/Status: All works completed. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2025, systematic plans for financially sustainable O&M prepared/updated by 3 ULBs (Coimbatore, Madurai and Thoothukudi) (2021 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: The systematic plans for Coimbatore and Madurai have been prepared and currently under review by respective corporations. Draft plan for Thoothukudi is also being prepared. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2026, 200 students, teachers, and administrators (at least 50% women); and at least 50% of members of three women groups reported improved awareness of water conservation and hygiene in Coimbatore, Thoothukudi, and Madurai (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: Preliminary activities are in progress (i.e., Activities [awareness generating activities for adolescent girls (on menstrual hygiene) and health and sanitation workers] were already initiated under the GAP and the consultation and participation plan). Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2026, improved knowledge on approaches to integrating gender in urban governancei, implementing gender action plans, and monitoring and reporting on gender equality results, reported by 60 ULB staff (including at least 30 women staff) (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 2.3.2) Progress/Status: Preliminary activities are in progress. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance strengthened Indicator: By 2026, new database on urban management for Thoothukudi established at the urban data and governance improvement cell in DMA, with sex-disaggregated data (2021 baseline: 0)h (OP 4.2.1) Progress/Status: Preliminary activities are in progress. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply system in one city (Madurai) improved with smart features. Indicator: 15 inline booster pumps with capacity of 70 kW installed in Madurai (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 4.1.2) Progress/Status: Works are ongoing (physical progress of 63.9% [total laid - 647.37 km] Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply system in one city (Madurai) improved with smart features. Indicator: A total of 813 km of new water distribution pipelines commissioned within 115 new district metered areas and metered connections provided to 163,958 households in Madurai (100% households, including poord households in coverage area) (2021 baseline: 0) (OP 2.1.4; OP 4.1.2) Progress/Status: 823.07 km (as per present site condition 908.17 km)of pipeline has been laid and 115865 HSC provided (as per present site condition 163958 Nos). Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:
